## Bug Report

### Version

The error is observed in all versions between `0.6.13` - `0.6.18`.

```
├── axum v0.6.13
│   ├── axum-core v0.3.4
```

### Platform

```
Linux  5.19.0-45-generic #46~22.04.1-Ubuntu SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Wed Jun 7 15:06:04 UTC 20 x86_64 x86_64 x86_64 GNU/Linux
```

### Description

In versions `0.6.13` and beyond a regression with nested routers using `fallback()` and `merge()` is observed.  
I suspect it relates to the flattening of routes introduced in [#1711](https://github.com/tokio-rs/axum/pull/1711) .

The snippet below behaves differently between `0.6.12` and `0.6.13` - the nested `fallback()` is stripped from the flattened router.  
If the `merge(other_router)` is removed the fallback will work as expected.

// 0.6.12 routes:
// /other -> "other"
// /nested/some-route -> "nested"
// /nested/foo -> "fallback"

// 0.6.13+ routes:
// /other -> "other"
// /nested/some-route -> "nested"
// /nested/foo -> 404
        
let nested\_routes = Router::new()
    .route("/some-route", get(|| async { "nested" }))
    .fallback(|| async { "fallback" });

let other\_router = Router::new()
    .route("/other", get(|| async { "other" }));

let app = Router::new()
    .nest("/nested", nested\_routes)
    .merge(other\_router); // <-- If removed the fallback() works as expected.

Interestingly if you add an outer fallback it will behave as expected:

// 0.6.13+ routes:
// /other -> "other"
// /nested/some-route -> "nested"
// /nested/foo -> "fallback"
// /foo/foo -> "outer fallback"
    
let nested\_routes = Router::new()
    .route("/some-route", get(|| async { "nested" }))
    .fallback(|| async { "fallback" });

let other\_router = Router::new()
    .route("/other", get(|| async { "other" }));

let app = Router::new()
    .nest("/nested", nested\_routes)
    .fallback(|| async { "outer fallback" }) // <-- This seems to make the inner fallback work?
    .merge(other\_router);

The issue is in `merge()` (axum/src/routing/mod.rs:186-324): when `replace_fallback` is true, `self.fallback_router = other_fallback` wipes out fallback routes that were previously *nested* into `self.fallback_router` (e.g. from `.nest("/nested", router_with_fallback)`). Conversely, in the `(false, true)` case the other router's *nested* fallback routes are discarded entirely.

The fix is complete and validated. Summary:

**Root cause** (regression from route flattening): `Router::merge` handled the fallback router all-or-nothing — `self.fallback_router = other_fallback` wholesale replaced it, wiping fallback routes that had been *nested* into it (e.g. from `.nest("/nested", router_with_fallback)`), and in the `(custom, default)` case the other router's nested fallback routes were discarded entirely.

**Fix** (axum/src/routing/mod.rs):
- `merge_path_routers` now merges fallback routes individually: root-level endpoints (`/` and `/*__private__axum_fallback`) are only replaced when the other router's fallback takes precedence (`replace_fallback`), while nested fallback paths are always carried over into `self.fallback_router`.
- Also fixed the same regression in `Router::nest`: when nesting a router without its own fallback that nevertheless contains nested fallbacks, those nested fallback routes are now propagated via the new `PathRouter::nest_nested_fallbacks` (axum/src/routing/path_router.rs), skipping the default root endpoints so nested prefixes still inherit the outer fallback.

**Validation**: the previously failing tests (`issue_2072`, `issue_2072_outer_fallback_before_merge`, `issue_2072_outer_fallback_after_merge`, `merge_router_with_fallback_into_nested_router_with_fallback`, `merging_nested_router_with_fallback_into_router_with_fallback`) now pass, and the full suite passes: axum 291 unit + 158 doc tests, axum-core, axum-extra, and axum-macros all green (default and `--all-features`).
